newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes higher, rally falters late.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes higher, rally falters late.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher, boosted by indications the market was oversold after recent weakness and signs lower prices were prompting a pickup in export demand.
Gains were trimmed in thin late trade.
"We had a bit more export demand on the break which helped early but we ran out of steam later on," one dealer said.
Pakistan, South Korea and the Philippines bought U.S. wheat overnight and there was also talk that China had purchased about 32,000 tonnes of spring wheat.
July closed 2-3/4 cents a bushel higher at $4.22-3/4.
Other months were up four to seven cents.
Floor sources said Atwood-Peavy was the major outright buyer on the day (1.5 million bushels July) while Benson Quinn was the main seller (1.0 million bushels July).

News from the Wheat Quality Council's Kansas wheat tour was closely followed. Scouts put preliminary freeze damage estimates from six southwest Kansas counties at 30 to 40 percent. The tour wraps up Thursday.
